evals.name: mcp-three-topics
evals.prompt: build me an artifact explaining these three topics for my course: MCP server transports (stdio vs HTTP), how tools/resources/prompts are declared by an MCP server, and how Claude Code discovers and loads .mcp.json
evals.expected_output: One RavTech-themed single-file HTML page with exactly three sections in the given order, each carrying real identifiers (JSON-RPC method names, .mcp.json keys), at least one real config/payload block, numbers/limits, and a trap. English only, dark-mode tokens intact, unverified claims flagged in the hand-off.

assertions.text: The page has exactly three top-level sections, one per requested topic, in the order the user listed them
Each section names real identifiers as the software spells them (tools/list, tools/call, resources/read; mcpServers, command, args, env, type/url)
Each section contains at least one real config file, payload or command block — not pseudo-code
The page states at least three concrete numbers (protocol version, timeout, scope count, size limit)
At least two traps or failure-path behaviours are called out explicitly
CSS declares the RavTech palette (#0a1f3d, #00c8ff, #ff7a00) and loads Heebo + Rubik + JetBrains Mono
Theme tokens are defined in bare :root, in a prefers-color-scheme:dark block guarded by :not([data-theme="light"]), and in :root[data-theme="dark"]
Code blocks scroll, tables sit in a scroll container, no min-width wider than 400px
English only, no leftover template text, lorem, or TODO markers
The hand-off lists the claims that could not be verified

evals.name: postgres-internals
evals.prompt: I need a technical explainer page on Postgres internals for engineers on my team: MVCC and tuple visibility, autovacuum tuning, and index-only scans / the visibility map
evals.expected_output: Same page contract on a subject outside Claude Code: three sections, real system column and GUC names, real SQL/EXPLAIN output, defaults and thresholds, and the traps (long transactions, wraparound, stale visibility map).

assertions.text: The page has exactly three top-level sections, one per requested topic, in the order the user listed them
Each section names real identifiers as Postgres spells them (xmin/xmax/ctid, autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor, pg_visibility, Heap Fetches)
Each section contains at least one real SQL statement, EXPLAIN output, or postgresql.conf snippet
The page states real defaults and thresholds (0.2 / 0.1 scale factors, threshold 50, 200 million freeze age)
At least two traps are called out (long transactions holding the xmin horizon, wraparound, stale visibility map)
CSS declares the RavTech palette (#0a1f3d, #00c8ff, #ff7a00) and loads Heebo + Rubik + JetBrains Mono
Theme tokens are defined in bare :root, in a prefers-color-scheme:dark block guarded by :not([data-theme="light"]), and in :root[data-theme="dark"]
Code blocks scroll, tables sit in a scroll container, no min-width wider than 400px
English only, no leftover template text, lorem, or TODO markers
The hand-off lists the claims that could not be verified
